issues.sym: Rough idle, white or gray haze at startup, hard starting, poor mileage, and an oil level that seems to rise as fuel leaks into the crankcase.
issues.why: The original injectors on this first Duramax crack or leak internally. Because they sit under the valve covers, leaking fuel thins the engine oil. GM replaced them with a revised design under extended coverage.
issues.next: Have a diesel shop run an injector balance test and an oil analysis. Fuel-thinned oil can wipe out bearings, so get it repaired before more driving or towing.

issues.t: Air leaks at the fuel filter head
issues.sym: Hard starting, stalling, stumbling under load, or a hand primer on the filter head that feels soft.
issues.why: The fuel filter housing can develop small cracks and its seals can shrink, letting air into a system that relies on suction to pull fuel from the tank.
issues.next: Have the filter head and seals checked for air leaks and replaced if needed. Re-prime the system correctly after any filter change.

issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a dropping coolant level, or the temperature creeping up while towing.
issues.why: The early Duramax water pump design tends to seep or fail at moderate mileage. GM fitted a larger, redesigned pump for 2006.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often and have any leak fixed early. If the gauge climbs, stop and let the engine cool; overheating a diesel can damage head gaskets.

issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs or a hot-engine warning comes on while towing or climbing long grades, especially in summer.
issues.why: The cooling system on early LLY trucks has little reserve, and a dirty radiator or intercooler, weak fan clutch or tired water pump pushes it over the edge. GM enlarged the radiator, fan and water pump for 2006.
issues.next: Ease off and let the engine cool if the gauge rises. Keep the radiator and intercooler fins clean and have the fan clutch, water pump and coolant checked before towing.

issues.sym: Misfires, rough running, a no-start, or injector or boost codes that come and go. It is often mistaken for bad injectors.
issues.why: The engine wiring harness can rub against brackets and engine parts until the insulation wears through, causing open or shorted circuits.
issues.next: Before replacing injectors, have the harness inspected for rubbed-through spots and repaired or re-routed.

issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, the brake warning light, brake fluid wet spots along the frame, or a pedal that suddenly goes much closer to the floor.
issues.why: In road-salt states the coating on the steel brake lines wears away and the lines rust through. NHTSA investigated these trucks; GM responded with pre-formed replacement line kits and a service bulletin rather than a recall.
issues.next: Have the brake lines inspected along the full frame, especially on older trucks from salt states. If the pedal sinks or fluid is leaking, do not drive it; have it towed.

issues.sym: A clunk or knock felt through the steering wheel when turning at low speed or over bumps, often worse in cold weather.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft that links the column to the steering gear loses its lubrication and binds, then releases with a clunk. GM issued bulletins to lubricate or replace the shaft.
issues.next: Mention the clunk at your next service and ask about GM bulletin 07-02-35-003. Get it checked sooner if steering feels loose or binds.

issues.t: Clogged diesel particulate filter and fuel-diluted oil
issues.sym: Frequent regeneration cycles, loss of power, black smoke, worse fuel mileage, and an oil level that rises between changes.
issues.why: The first Duramax with a particulate filter burns off soot by injecting extra fuel. Short trips and stop-and-go use keep the filter loaded, and some of that extra fuel washes into the oil.
issues.next: Take regular highway drives so regenerations can finish, keep oil changes on time, and have the filter and sensors checked if power drops or smoke appears.

issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, stalling, or a no-start, sometimes after a period of hard starting and low fuel pressure codes.
issues.why: The Bosch CP4 pump can wear internally and send metal through the injectors and fuel rails, which can ruin the whole high-pressure system. It was the subject of a class-action settlement, and GM switched pumps for 2017.
issues.next: Change fuel filters on schedule and drain water from the separator. If the engine starts losing power, stop driving and tow it in rather than restarting it over and over.

issues.t: NOx sensor and DEF system faults
issues.sym: Check engine light, DEF or emissions warnings, and a countdown to reduced speed or reduced power.
issues.why: The NOx sensors, DEF level sensor, DEF pump and DEF tank heater on this first urea-equipped Duramax fail often. A bad heater can let the fluid freeze in very cold weather.
issues.next: Have the codes read promptly. Fix the fault before the truck limits its speed, and ask the dealer whether any extended emissions coverage applies.

issues.t: Rear fuel tank can collapse and starve the engine (recall)
issues.eng: 6.6L Duramax L5P diesel with dual tanks
issues.sym: The engine stumbles or stalls when the front tank runs low, the fuel gauge reads wrong, the rear tank level never seems to drop, or the truck is slow to start.
issues.why: A clogged vent on the optional rear tank lets suction build while fuel is pumped forward. The tank can collapse and stop feeding the front tank.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V-047. Until it is fixed, do not let the front tank run low.

issues.t: Engine block heater cord can short and overheat (recall)
issues.eng: 6.6L Duramax L5P diesel with block heater
issues.sym: A burning smell or a melted or scorched plug at the block heater cord, or a block heater that stops warming the engine.
issues.why: The block heater cord can short internally, which creates a fire risk while it is plugged in.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 19V-328 and 21V-496. Do not plug in the block heater until the cord has been inspected or replaced.

issues.sym: The hood does not latch firmly, rattles, or flutters at highway speed.
issues.why: The hood latch striker can fail, so the hood could open while driving and block the view ahead. A second recall covered trucks not repaired correctly the first time.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 20V-142 and 20V-324. If the hood flutters or will not latch, do not drive on the highway until it is repaired.

issues.sym: A sudden harsh downshift or the rear wheels locking up while moving, which can cause a skid. After the repair, a warning light, reduced-power message or firm shifting can signal the problem is developing.
issues.why: Wear in the transmission's control valve body can leak fluid pressure and move valves unexpectedly, often on a downshift from eighth gear. GM added software that watches for the wear, and some 2020 trucks were recalled again because the first fix did not cover them.
issues.next: Look up the VIN for open recalls, including the follow-up campaign, and have the repair done as soon as possible. If a transmission warning appears, have it checked before driving further.

issues.t: Power tailgate can unlatch by itself (recall)
issues.sym: The tailgate is found open after parking or drops open without anyone touching it, sometimes while driving.
issues.why: Water can get into the outside release switch on the power-release tailgate and short it, sending a false open signal. A second recall added more 2024 trucks and a better-sealed switch.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 24V-060 and 24V-894. Avoid carrying loose items in the bed until it is fixed.

issues.sym: A clunk or looseness in the steering, or the truck not responding normally to steering input.
issues.why: A shaft in the steering gear can fracture, which could cause a loss of steering control.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V-549. If the steering clunks or feels loose, stop driving and have the truck towed to a dealer.
